text: Dún Bolg is a legendary place of battle in County Wicklow. Here the warriors of Leinster showed their resistance to the bórama, the cow tribute they were forced to pay to the king of Tara. The story resembles the Trojan Horse. Disguised warriors hid inside baskets hung from the backs of the tribute cows. The cows carried the warriors into the king's camp, where they burst out and battled the king's men into submission. Koch records a separate battle of Dún Bolg in 598, in which the king Aed mac Ainmirech died.

okr.objective: Document Dún Bolg as the Leinster battle site tied to the bórama cow tribute.
